⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering

Highlights

  • − BigQuery users of the Storage API v1beta1 face its shutdown on August 31, 2027, after which calls fail with a NOT_FOUND error; the note says to migrate to the v1 API and update connectors and client libraries to versions defaulting to v1 by then.
  • − Holders of legacy OpenSharing open recipient tokens issued before February 25, 2026 (expiring after February 25, 2027 or with no expiration) now auto-expire on February 25, 2027; Databricks recommends rotating them before then.
  • BigQuery users of the AI.PREDICT and AI.EVALUATE functions now default to TabFM version 1.1 (Preview), which raises input limits to 80,000 sampled training rows and 128 feature columns.

Action required

Date Item Platform What to do
2026-11-30 Upcoming end of life for the Genie One MCP Beta endpoint Azure Databricks The Genie One MCP Beta endpoint at https://<workspace-hostname>/api/2.0/mcp/genie reaches end of life on November 30, 2026, after which requests fail; migrate all workloads to the system.ai.genie_one_mcp MCP in Unity Gateway.

2027-02-25 Latest automatic expiration date for legacy OpenSharing open recipient tokens moved to February 25, 2027 Azure Databricks Recommended: rotate these tokens before February 25, 2027: OpenSharing open recipient tokens issued before February 25, 2026, with expiration dates after February 25, 2027, or with no expiration now auto-expire on February 25, 2027 (previously December 8, 2026), and rotated tokens use the new recipient-specific URL format.

Databricks

Date Item Summary

Quiet today: Snowpark Python, Snowflake Connector for Python, Apache Polaris, Terraform provider for Snowflake

Azure / Fabric & GCP

Date Item Summary
2026-11-25 ⚠️ The BigQuery Storage API v1beta1 is deprecated and will be shut down on August 31, 2027 Migrate workloads from v1beta1 to v1 by August 31, 2027: after that date calls to the v1beta1 endpoint fail with a NOT_FOUND error, so update connectors and client libraries to versions that default to the v1 API.

Soda Core

  • Release: v4.32.0 fixes contract handling by refusing two data sources with one name.

Weekly Diff 2026-11-23

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟧 AI Policy · 🟨 Data Engineering · ⬜ Weekly Diff · 🟫 Trends

Items: 376 | Sources: the pages of 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-23 | Written by claude-opus-5-5 | Text in italics is interpretation | Generated: 2026-11-23 07:21 UTC

OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol reached coding agents this week, and two agents made Sol their default selection. Several reports this week concerned prompts leaking from inference providers, including a Together AI notice to customers about prompts sent to its serverless inference service in June and July 2026. On the data side, Azure Databricks retired Gemini 3.6 Flash on 2026-11-19 and set further retirement dates, while Databricks and Snowflake changed several defaults.

GPT-6.2 in the coding agents

OpenRouter's listing calls GPT-6.2 Sol an upgrade to GPT-6.1 Sol, positioned below GPT-6.2 Astra in the series. Codex 0.171.0 added both models to its catalogs, with Sol as the default catalog selection. Pi v1.6.0 made GPT-6.2 Sol the default for its openai, azure and openai-codex providers instead of GPT-6.1 Sol, at the same price. It also notes that both models reject reasoning effort none and minimal, so thinking level off is unavailable.

Caching needed a fix. OpenCode v2.3.2 says GPT-6.2 models don't cache a system prompt sent in the Responses instructions field, so every step re-billed it as uncached input. OpenCode now sends that prompt as a leading developer message. By its own figure, uncached input per step on GitHub Copilot gpt-6.2-sol dropped from about 14,000 tokens to 3. Oh My Pi v19.1.0 now sends GPT-6.2 system prompts as leading developer messages through third-party Responses proxies.

Not every path works yet. An Oh My Pi issue reports GPT-6.2 Sol missing from its Codex model list and rejected with model_not_found, while the native Codex CLI works. The reporter writes that the cause is not established.

In OpenRouter's one-day snapshot of top models on 2026-11-22, openai/gpt-6.1-sol-20260929 fell to #19 from #10 the week before. tencent/hy4-flash-20261116 entered the table at #4 with 10.21T tokens.

Separately, an issue on Claude Code reports premium Team and Enterprise seats using up their limits about 3–5x faster on non-Fable models since roughly the week of 2026-11-09. The reporter says everyone in their organization on premium seats sees the same drop.

The OpenCode figure suggests that, for GPT-6.2, where a harness places the system prompt can decide most of the per-step input bill. Harnesses that pass it in instructions are worth checking. The GPT-6.1 Sol drop is a single day's figure, and whether GPT-6.2 takes over that traffic is worth watching.

Prompts leaking from inference providers

OpenRouter says it off-boarded three providers. It also removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility and notified potentially affected customers, after canary token research on inference providers. In a separate write-up, Dragos says it seeded two million AI prompts with canary tokens. It reports finding three provider breaches, prompt theft and ignored Zero Data Retention settings.

The package supply chain also had an incident. Socket's write-up on agent-framework says compromised versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 on PyPI use .pth startup hooks to exfiltrate Azure, GitHub Actions and CI/CD credentials.

Disclosure timelines are also changing. Anthropic says frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. It is shortening its disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all others. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported on or after 2027-01-01.

This suggests Zero Data Retention eligibility is a per-endpoint status that can change while a client relies on it. For EU work built on it, the list of eligible endpoints is worth watching. From 2027, Anthropic's shorter windows would also leave maintainers less time between a report and its disclosure.

Retirements and changed defaults in data platforms

The Genie One MCP Beta endpoint at /api/2.0/mcp/genie reaches end of life on 2026-11-30, after which requests fail. Its replacement is the system.ai.genie_one_mcp MCP in Unity Gateway. Azure Databricks retires GPT-5 and GPT-5 mini on 2026-12-11 and recommends GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra as replacements.

Several query and streaming results will change:

  • array_contains: Starting on or after 2027-01-15, with ANSI mode enabled in Databricks Runtime 19 and above, array_contains will return NULL instead of false for a constant empty array and a NULL value. As a result, NOT array_contains will no longer match those rows.
  • Streaming watermarks: In Databricks Runtime 19, new streaming queries in real-time mode use real-time watermark propagation by default, so state is evicted sooner. Queries restarted from an existing checkpoint keep their original behavior.
  • Output policies: Model output policies now default to streaming evaluation, including existing policies, and released text can't be recalled. This feature is in Beta.
  • Snowflake dynamic tables: Snowflake's AUTO refresh mode for dynamic tables now resolves to ADAPTIVE instead of INCREMENTAL when the definition supports incremental refresh.

Dagster 1.13.31 also has a breaking change: its Claude Code plugin no longer reads DAGSTER_CLOUD_MCP_URL. Organizations in the EU region must add the EU server directly, or the plugin connects to the US server and authentication fails.

Several of these changes alter results without raising an error: a NULL in place of false, earlier state eviction, and streamed text that can't be recalled. Those are the changes a test suite is least likely to flag. The Dagster change is the one that directly affects EU-region setups.

EU and Dutch regulators

The Commission is collecting feedback on a draft template for a questionnaire. The template is meant to help certain deployers of high-risk AI systems prepare a fundamental rights impact assessment under Article 27 of the AI Act. For 2026-12-02, the AI Act timeline lists bans on sexual deepfakes and CSAM generators, and the end of the Art. 50(2) transition.

The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens advises consumers against buying AI camera glasses for general use. In its own study of six such glasses, one wrongly said an ambulance was on its way during a simulated resuscitation. The AP also found security problems in the software.

Politico Europe reports that an Irish regulator stopped X from training AI with data gathered by agents. The regulator says it has significant concerns about personal data being collected by AI agents. In the Tweede Kamer, an amended motion asks for an inventory of what is needed to supervise the AI Act.

The Irish case and the AP study both concern data that agents or devices collect about people other than the user. This suggests that is where regulator attention fell this week for agent projects at EU clients.

Research

Paper Summary
NariQ: Sub-3-Bit Quantization for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks NariQ is a trellis-coded post-training quantization method that calibrates on tokens the BF16 model generates during agent sessions; it targets the finding that existing ≤3-bit quantizations of Qwen3.8-27B match BF16 on AIME but solve at most 72% as many DeepSWE tasks, though the truncated abstract gives no NariQ result.
LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that runs on local hardware as a fast "System 1" gate and escalates to a slower LLM agent (System 2), offloading work from hosted agents such as a Claude Opus 5.5 agent that costs over $70,000 a year at 10,000 queries a day, though the truncated abstract reports no accuracy or savings results.
Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution Linglong Agent Service (agentsvc) is a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime where a parent service keeps inference orchestration, tool descriptions and conversation history, while each inference request picks one child environment for file, shell, terminal and MCP operations, though the truncated abstract reports no evaluation results.
